title: The release evidence and its receipt are readable over HTTP, so the browser can show what it is approving
description:
PREREQUISITE ROW filed by worker-deb4c7d8 on 2026-09-06 from inside task-817d893fa1254a4d82d2888af1f87a47 (the Gate 3 browser proof), whose step-1 measurement found this gap. Parent: task-817d893fa1254a4d82d2888af1f87a47, which now declares dependsOn against this row. Filed under global rail 4 clause 2 (a proof row's missing capability becomes a prerequisite PRODUCTION row with the gap measured symbol by symbol, never a mock-backed journey) and global rail 20 (spun-out rows are filed in PLANNING).

THE GAP: `release.decide` IS OFFERED AND SERVED, BUT NOTHING RELEASE-SHAPED IS READABLE. Measured at HEAD 57446237 on moe/work-2026-09-04, four ways:

(1) NO ROUTE. `JSON_ROUTES` (http-listener-read-dispatch.ts:73-107) has 31 members and none is release-shaped. `git grep -n "release" -- apps/daemon/src/http/*.ts` minus tests returns ONLY the two offer lines in affordance-planning-offers.ts (:148, :294) plus goal-deployment-read.ts.

(2) THE BROWSER HAS ONE RELEASE DATUM, AND IT IS AN ID. `goal-deployment-read.ts:41` puts `releaseDecision: release?.ok === true ? release.receipt.receiptId : null` on the DEPLOYMENTS read, decoded at `apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments.ts:7`. It is a receipt ID only, and only for a RELEASED receipt — `:35-36` reads `releaseReceiptId(projectId, goalRef, sha, "RELEASED", null)`, so a REFUSED receipt is invisible by construction. `prUrl`, `refusalCode` and `dossierSha256` are on `ReleaseReceiptV1` (release-receipt-contracts.ts:28-39) and reach no reader.

(3) THE DOSSIER IS PERSISTED AS MARKDOWN ONLY. `ReleaseDossierV1` (release-dossier-contracts.ts:98-105) is `{dossierId, goalId, markdown, projectId, sha, version}`. The STRUCTURED evidence — `CriterionRow`, `DossierGap`, `DossierGapCode` and the `UNKNOWN` sentinel (release-dossier.ts:6, :28, :56-119) — is computed inside `renderReleaseDossier`/`releaseDossierGaps`, rendered into the markdown, and never persisted or served in structured form.

(4) `runs-read.ts` HAS NO RELEASE MEMBER AT ALL (`git grep -n "release" -- apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.ts` returns nothing), so the Runs feed cannot show a release receipt.

WHY THIS BLOCKS THE PROOF ROW. task-817d893f's DoD 1 requires the card to render criteria covered n/m WITH THE UNKNOWN COUNT SHOWN SEPARATELY; its task rail 2 says folding UNKNOWN into covered "defeats child 1's whole design", and the row's own description calls it "the worst defect this row could ship". With no structured read, the only way to compute that number in the browser is to PARSE THE MARKDOWN — which makes the card a second authority for exactly the number that must never be wrong. DoD 2's `prUrl` link and DoD 4's "Runs shows the release receipt" have no source at all.

WHAT THIS ROW SHOULD DELIVER (the architect sizes and seams it; this is the measured need, not a design):
- A structured release read for one goal, served on a new JSON_ROUTES member and registered in EVERY seam the roster demands (the explicit dispatch branch, `apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts`, and the bidirectional roster arm in http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts, which must pass WITHOUT an exemption).
- Its answer carries what the card must show: the criterion rows with their UNKNOWN gaps kept DISTINCT from covered ones (the `DossierGap`/`UNKNOWN` distinction preserved on the wire, never collapsed), the verifier receipts and landing shas, the preview decision or its explicit absence, and the release receipt's `outcome`, `prUrl`, `refusalCode` and `dossierSha256` for BOTH the RELEASED and the REFUSED receipt.
- A decision, made deliberately and written at the site, about whether the structured evidence is DERIVED at read time from `releaseDossierGaps` or PERSISTED alongside the markdown. Deriving keeps one authority; persisting keeps the read cheap. Either is defensible; an undocumented choice is not.
- The read is a READ: it must not mint, decide, or move any aggregate.

NOT IN SCOPE: the Release card, its arms and the browser journey (task-817d893f owns them); the `release.decide` kind and its service (task-f961dc89, DONE); the dossier itself (task-70a7ccd3, DONE); the affordance offer (task-2120955202764428a53be598d0f149b4, landed 57446237).

ONE ADJACENT FINDING, recorded here because the next reader will hit it and it may or may not belong to this row — the architect decides. `offer-wire.ts:41-47 refusalOf` in the control-room reads only `code` and `layer` from a daemon refusal and DROPS `detail`. The daemon does send the authority's own words: `releaseRefusal` carries `detail` (release-decide-contracts.ts:83-93), `domainRefusalOf` (daemon-command-dispatch.ts:54-61) puts it on the wire deliberately ("one real planning seat bisected seven graph shapes against a refusal whose cause it was never told"), and `release-decide-service.ts:160-161` answers `unverified evidence for: ${criteria}` with the criterion ids. So today those ids reach the browser and are discarded one layer before any card can render them. task-817d893f's DoD 2 requires them to reach the operator, and `offer-wire.ts` is shared by every decision card, so it is not obviously that row's to change.
definitionOfDone: A structured release read is SERVED for one goal on a new route, registered in every seam: the JSON_ROUTES roster AND an explicit dispatch branch (a member without one is silently served by the dossier handler), plus apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts so the dev lane can reach it. The bidirectional roster arm in http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts MUST pass WITHOUT an exemption entry — if it demands one, the branch is missing; fix the branch, never the arm.

THE UNKNOWN DISTINCTION SURVIVES THE WIRE, asserted directly: a goal whose dossier carries an unmeasurable criterion answers with that criterion DISTINGUISHABLE from a covered one, and a consumer can compute covered n/m and the UNKNOWN count SEPARATELY without parsing markdown. A test asserts the two counts against a dossier built with at least one gap and at least one covered criterion — equal counts would let the arm pass while the distinction was lost.

THE RECEIPT'S OPERATOR-FACING FIELDS ARE READABLE FOR BOTH OUTCOMES: `outcome`, `prUrl`, `refusalCode` and `dossierSha256` for a RELEASED receipt AND for a REFUSED one. goal-deployment-read.ts:35-36 reads only the RELEASED id today, so a refused release is invisible; assert the REFUSED case explicitly, because that is the one the operator most needs to see.

The read is a READ: it commits nothing and moves no aggregate version. Assert the goal's and the release aggregate's versions are unchanged across the call - a read that writes would erase the goal from durableGoals exactly as a mistargeted decide would.

The derive-vs-persist choice is made deliberately and WRITTEN AT THE SITE, naming which authority computes the criterion rows and why. If derived at read time, say what bounds the cost per poll (the affordance hot-path incident of 2026-09-05 is the precedent); if persisted, say what keeps it in step with the markdown.

Refusals carry a stable code WITH its layer, asserted together - never merely that the read failed. An unreadable dossier and an absent one are DIFFERENT answers and the card renders them differently. NEVER COLLAPSE UNKNOWN INTO COVERED ON THE WIRE. The dossier deliberately renders unmeasurable evidence as UNKNOWN and LISTS it rather than dropping it; a read that flattens the distinction defeats the whole design and puts an operator one step from approving evidence nobody measured.

A NEW JSON ROUTE IS A THREE-SEAM EDIT (roster, explicit dispatch branch, dev-proxy pin) and the bidirectional roster arm is the check that all three happened. Register the UNCONSUMED-ROUTE census entry NAMING task-817d893fa1254a4d82d2888af1f87a47 as the row that retires it - a served route with no consumer is a known, named state here, not an accident.

THE READ MUST NOT MINT. Reads on this surface are pure; the release aggregate carries dossier writes and decide decisions, and any commit from a read path risks the last-write-wins hazard that erases a goal from durableGoals.

Confirm both, since step 2 exports the first and step 5 creates a suite for the second.

Record the five gate baselines. If (b) comes out differently — a second sha authority, or a release decided at a sha the publication read does not know — STOP and report: the read would answer about a different release than the one the operator approves.

**EXPORT THE ROWS, THEN BUILD THE READ.** Two files.

(1) `apps/daemon/src/release/release-dossier.ts` — export `criterionRows` (or a thin named wrapper over it). ONE LINE OF PRODUCTION CHANGE, and the justification is already written in that file at :140-154: "A caller that needs to NAME what is missing reads this rather than the stored dossier: `ReleaseDossierV1` keeps only the rendered markdown, so re-parsing the document back into rows would reimplement this authority against a prose artefact." That sentence is this row's derive-vs-persist answer, written by the module that owns the derivation.

(2) NEW `apps/daemon/src/http/release-read.ts`, modelled on `preview-read.ts` and kept UNDER 250 LINES. `RELEASE_READ_PATH = "/release/read"`. A module-private `const LAYER = "RELEASE_READ"` — NOT `RELEASE_READ_LAYER`: the boundary roster's `[A-Z0-9_]+(?:LAYER|LAYERS|BOUNDARIES)` shape is reserved for security boundaries and the `_LAYER` tail would demand a roster backfill (preview-read.ts:45-48 states this discipline).

THE ENVELOPE IS THE PRECEDENT'S, and it is load-bearing: `ABSENT` | `PRESENT` | `REFUSED`, because "this goal has no release evidence yet" is NOT a fault and a card that cannot tell it from one renders an error for the ordinary case.

**THE UNKNOWN DISTINCTION IS THE PRODUCT (DoD 2).** The projection carries the criterion rows with `gaps` INTACT per row — never a boolean, never a pre-summed pair. Let the consumer count; a `covered`/`unknown` pair computed here would become a second authority the card could disagree with, and a row whose gaps were flattened to a count cannot say WHICH citation failed or why. `DossierGap` already carries `{code, criterionId, detail}` — forward all three.

**THE GAPS PATH IS THE CASE THAT MATTERS AND IT HAS NO STORED DOSSIER.** `release-production-wiring.ts` returns `{input, ancestry}` WITHOUT recording a dossier whenever `releaseDossierGaps(...)` is non-empty, so a goal with gaps has NOTHING stored. A read that served only stored dossiers would answer ABSENT for exactly the goals whose UNKNOWN count the operator most needs. So DERIVE: `readReleaseDossierInput` + the ancestry predicate + `criterionRows`, the same three the decide edge uses.

Also project the receipt for BOTH outcomes (`outcome`, `prUrl`, `refusalCode`, `dossierSha256`, `receiptId`, `sha`) by the ledger walk step 1(c) named, and the goal's landed sha. NAMED MEMBERS ONLY in the projection (preview-read.ts's `projectionOf` discipline): a key the receipt grows later must not leak through.

READ-ONLY, and say so at the top: nothing here commits, records or decides. In particular do NOT call `recordReleaseDossier` — the decide edge records; a read that wrote would move the release aggregate under the offer the card is holding.

Refusing would hide the criteria entirely; folding silently would tell an operator their evidence had FAILED when in truth nothing measured it. The flag is how the card tells those two apart, and it is why I added a member the DoD did not name.

**THE WORLD, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, and this is the part the plan got wrong.** The plan said to build the world with `openStore` + `driveThrough` + `seedLandingReceipt`, the way my affordance arms did. I probed it before writing anything: **`readReleaseDossierInput` returns NULL in that world** — the bootstrap seed journey has publish requests but no APPROVED PRODUCT CONTRACT SCOPE, and scope is what the dossier folds. The bound planning world (`boundWorld` + `committedRevision` + `approveGate1` + `submit` + `approvePlan`, as `release-durable-facts.test.ts` uses) has scope but no publish request. Neither world alone can exercise this read. The suite therefore uses the planning world AND writes a real publication into it.

**THE MIXED FIXTURE, which is the row's whole point.** The default plan structure puts BOTH criteria on ONE node, so every criterion always shares one verdict and covered/UNKNOWN can never differ — an arm built on it would pass just as happily against a projection that had collapsed the distinction. `structureOf` takes a node list, so the world submits TWO nodes (`node-api` carrying `crit-api`, `node-ui` carrying `crit-ui`) and accepts + lands evidence for ONE. Result: `covered === 1`, `unknown === 1` — non-zero and different from each other, exactly as DoD 2 demands. The arm also asserts the gap's `code` AND `criterionId` (`["RECEIPT_ABSENT", "LANDING_ABSENT"]` on `crit-ui`), because a count alone cannot tell an operator what to go and fix.
